record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.original_question: How should oscillation analyses reconstruct the incident neutrino energy in CCQE-like events when only the outgoing lepton or an incomplete hadronic final state is measured, given Fermi motion, scattering from correlated nucleon pairs, finite detection thresholds, limited neutron detection, flux uncertainties, and model-dependent multinucleon effects that can bias the mapping between true and reconstructed energy?

evidence.quote:
From this body of work, it is clear that the extracted distribution of incident
neutrino energies for a given measured charged lepton momentum greatly de-
pends on the energy distribution of the incident neutrino ﬂux, which typically
has signiﬁcant uncertainties. If it were possible to measure the energy of all
the ﬁnal state particles, in addition to the outgoing lepton, it would be possible
in principle to unambiguously assign a neutrino energy by exploiting energy
conservation. Practically, all detectors have ﬁnite energy thresholds for particle
detection and other limitations ( e.g. detection of ﬁnal state neutrons) that will
induce errors that depend on the accuracy of the underlying physics models.

Using the momentum of the
ﬁnal state muon to infer the incident neutrino energy can greatly underestimate
that energy if the muon was produced by CCQE scattering oﬀ a neutron in a
correlated pair. The correlated pair can be viewed as being far oﬀ-shell and the
scattering interaction must put both nucleons back on-shell.

However, a wider range of models need to be explored, and as the
precision of the measurement increases as more data is accumulated at T2K, a
more detailed analysis will be necessary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) neutrino–nucleus scattering events of the form ν_ℓ + A → ℓ^- + X, where the incoming neutrino has unknown energy E_ν drawn from a flux distribution Φ(E_ν) with significant uncertainty, and the target nucleus contains nucleons subject to Fermi motion as well as short-range correlated nucleon pairs whose constituents are appreciably off the mass shell. Assume that detectors observe the outgoing lepton four-momentum p_ℓ exactly, but observe the hadronic final state only partially: each final-state hadron of species s is detected with probability depending on its kinetic energy through a threshold function (in particular, final-state neutrons are largely undetected), and additional final-state interactions and multinucleon (2p2h) processes — described by a family of competing nuclear models {M_α} — can produce additional unobserved nucleons.

Under these conditions, design a procedure (a deterministic estimator or a posterior reconstruction) that maps the observed event data to a reconstructed neutrino energy Ê_ν such that the bias and variance of Ê_ν − E_ν are controlled uniformly over (i) the flux uncertainty in Φ, (ii) the Fermi-motion distribution of the struck nucleon, (iii) the contribution of scattering off correlated nucleon pairs (which, when treated as single-nucleon CCQE using only the lepton kinematics, systematically underestimates E_ν because both nucleons of the pair must be put on-shell), (iv) finite detection thresholds and missing neutron information, and (v) the choice of multinucleon model M_α.

Specifically: give an explicit reconstruction prescription, together with quantitative bounds on its model-dependence, that an oscillation analysis (which infers oscillation parameters from the reconstructed-energy spectrum) can use without introducing biases larger than its statistical precision; or prove that no such prescription exists, identifying the minimal additional measurement (e.g., specified hadronic observables above specified thresholds) required to make the mapping from true to reconstructed neutrino energy unambiguous.
artifact.status_search_result: Neutrino energy reconstruction in CCQE-like events remains an active and unresolved problem in neutrino physics. Recent literature (T2K, NOvA, MicroBooNE, DUNE generator and theory studies through 2024–2025) continues to report model-dependent biases from 2p2h/multinucleon effects, Fermi motion, and missing neutrons, with no universally accepted unbiased estimator; mitigation via transverse-kinematic-imbalance variables and improved nuclear models is partial.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino energy reconstruction and the shape of the CCQE-like total cross section
status_evidence.snippet: Multinucleon effects can produce significant biases in the reconstructed neutrino energy spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that multinucleon contributions bias reconstructed Eν in CCQE-like analyses.

status_evidence.title: Transverse kinematic imbalance and neutrino energy reconstruction (recent reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ongoing efforts to control nuclear-model dependence in oscillation analyses; problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Energy reconstruction bias from nuclear effects is still being studied; not solved.
